limitations: Simulation-only; cracker is equilibrium/kinetic model without reported kinetic parameters (k0, E0, beta not given).
Eq. (2) exponent on p_NH3 printed as 3 (classic Temkin-Pyzhev form uses 2); k vs k0 naming inconsistent.
R1 and Eq. (4) print (2+alpha)/2 O2; the balanced value is (2+alpha)/4 (confirmed from PDF image).
Table 2 labels the cracker 'adiabatic' while it is exhaust-heated; p. 3 says equilibrium while p. 5 says kinetic PFR.
Fig. 19(b) equilibrium conversions are systematically above an ideal-gas equilibrium cross-check (e.g. 96.4 % vs 93.1 % at 500 degC/30 bar) - do not use as equilibrium benchmark.
Cracker heat duty, capacity factor and cracking-temperature sensitivity are only in the Supplementary Material (not reviewed).
CAPEX correlation is an SMR-analogy fit with unstated cost year; NH3 cracking TRL 4-6.
Conclusion attributes 58.6 MW to PR 8 although Sec. 3.3 reports it for PR 30 / cracking at 5 bar.
relevance: Economics and process context for AmCraX: complete LCOE methodology (CEPCI scaling with CEPCI_2024 = 800.3, sum f = 2.06, CRF with r = 10 %, t = 25 y, maintenance 2.5 % and insurance 2 % of TCI, labour correlation) and an NH3 cracker CAPEX correlation CAPEX[MUSD] = 18.171*Size[t-H2/h]^0.7451 usable as literature-sourced economic inputs (original data Cesaro et al. 2021). NH3 price points 480 / 320 USD/t. Exhaust-heated Ru cracker at 500 degC / 10 bar with dT_min 5 K; shows lower cracking pressure increases conversion and outweighs recompression - relevant to the AmCraX pressure sensitivity. Topsoe 500 t/d H2 commercial cracker as scale reference. Not a valid equilibrium benchmark (Fig. 19b discrepancy).
